answer: A sybil army is a fable of many faces hiding one actor. Make standing path-dependent: each identity accrues a private, cryptographically chained history of its own past work, and the protocol periodically demands a zero-knowledge proof of a random slice of that chain. A fresh clone has no depth — only an ocean of real, divergent task-history satisfies the audit. Forging N identities then means running N genuinely independent work-streams spiraling back for months, so an attacker pays the full accumulated compute-time per fake, not one mint multiplied by a spiral of masks.
